title: Creamy Butternut Squash Gnocchi with Spinach, Sweet Peas & Ricotta
summary: A dairy vegetarian dinner of pillowy potato gnocchi tossed in a light ricotta-garlic sauce with roasted butternut squash, wilted spinach and sweet peas. 35–40 minutes total, 20–25 minutes active; kid-friendly components can be served separately.
ingredients: 2 lb kosher-certified potato gnocchi (check dairy status and ingredients)
2 cups peeled butternut squash, diced into ½-inch cubes
½ cup milk or unsalted vegetable broth, plus a splash if needed
½ tsp dried sage or thyme
1 tsp lemon zest and 1 tsp lemon juice (optional)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss ½-inch squash cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a sheet pan and roast 20–25 minutes until tender, turning once.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. When the squash has about 10 minutes left, cook gnocchi according to package instructions (usually 2–4 minutes, until they float); reserve ½ cup cooking water and drain.
While gnocchi cooks, warm 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Cook minced garlic 30–60 seconds without browning. Add peas and ¼ cup water; cover and heat for 3 minutes.

Turn heat to low. Stir in ricotta and ½ cup milk or vegetable broth until a loose sauce forms. Add spinach and stir until wilted, about 1–2 minutes. Thin with reserved gnocchi water as needed; season with sage or thyme, salt and pepper.
Fold in gnocchi and roasted squash gently. Finish with optional lemon zest and a few drops of lemon juice. Serve warm.
child_friendly_modifications: Reserve plain gnocchi before saucing and serve with a small spoonful of ricotta for dipping. Offer sweet peas and soft roasted squash in separate piles; chop spinach finely or keep it in the adult sauce. Cut large gnocchi pieces in half for the 3-year-old.
leftovers: Refrigerate promptly within 2 hours; eat within 3–4 days. Reheat gently in a skillet with a splash of milk or water to loosen the sauce. Pack separate roasted squash and peas for easy lunches.
